questions.q: A baby delivered with the arm pulled upward develops claw hand with Horner's syndrome on that side. The lesion is in the:
opts: lower trunk of the brachial plexus (C8–T1)
upper trunk of the brachial plexus (C5–C6)
questions.why: This is Klumpke's palsy; T1 involvement interrupts the sympathetic outflow to the head, giving Horner's syndrome.

questions.q: When a new dissimilar disease has acted on the organism for long and joins the old one, each occupying its own region, Hahnemann (§40) calls the result:
questions.why: §40: dissimilar diseases may unite into a complex disease, each occupying its own locality in the organism; allopathic drugging commonly produces this.

questions.q: The standards of the HPI become legally binding because the Drugs and Cosmetics Act names the HPI in its:
questions.why: The Second Schedule of the Act lists the standards drugs must meet; for homoeopathic medicines it names the HPI (and, failing that, other official homoeopathic pharmacopoeias).

questions.q: According to §6, the unprejudiced observer perceives in each individual disease only:
opts: the changes in health of body and mind that can be perceived by the senses
the material cause of the disease
the name given to the disease in textbooks
questions.why: §6: the observer, free from speculation, notices only deviations from the former healthy state, felt by the patient, remarked by those around him and observed by the physician.

questions.q: According to §85, while recording the case the physician should:
opts: group the symptoms under the diagnosis
write the symptoms in order of their severity
begin a fresh line with every new symptom, so each stands separately
record only the symptoms that seem important
questions.why: §85: a fresh line for each new circumstance, symptoms ranged separately one below the other, so each can be completed later.

questions.q: Hahnemann's essay 'Aesculapius in the Balance' (1805) was:
opts: a critique of the medicine of his time
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. It questioned the certainty of medicine.

questions.q: Under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, a drug sold under the name of another drug, or falsely claiming to be made by a certain manufacturer, is termed:
questions.why: Section 17-B defines spurious drugs (imitations and false claims of identity or maker); 17 covers misbranding and 17-A adulteration.

questions.q: Under the national programme, the first dose of vitamin A given at 9 months of age is:
questions.why: The first dose is 1 lakh IU at 9 months with MR; later doses are 2 lakh IU every 6 months up to 5 years.

questions.q: Rheumatism that begins in the feet and travels upwards is characteristic of:
questions.why: Ledum: rheumatism begins in the feet and ascends; Kalmia's pains travel downward (Boericke).

questions.q: The abbreviation 'h.s.' on a prescription means:
questions.why: 'h.s.' (hora somni) means at bedtime, which is not among options A to D.
